environment.machine: macOS (Apple Silicon), local out-of-source build root-build-tagma
environment.dataset_note: CMS Run2016G DoubleMuon NanoAOD, tree Events, 2,315,223 events, 2,155,974,646 bytes, downloaded from eospublic.cern.ch

method.workload: read every event of the dataset through TTree::GetEntry, cache disabled in the baseline (M1 workload)
method.baseline: ordinary ROOT read path, no store attached
method.coordinate: TTagmaStore attached, one aligned fixed-width record read per event
method.coordinate_map: TTagmaStore::MapFile, record copied from the mapped store file, zero read system calls
method.metrics: wall seconds, cpu seconds, read calls, tagma-served calls, read syscalls (TFile::GetSysReadCalls), bytes moved (TFile::GetBytesRead delta)

synthetic_20k.note: synthetic scattered tree with the same per-event payload, local files, 20,000 events, 3 branches per event, cache disabled

real_same_media_2k.note: local NanoAOD file, 2,000 events, cache disabled, M1 signature slice (1.37 reads per event)

real_same_media_full.note: local NanoAOD file, all 2,315,223 events, cache disabled, the full-dataset same-media comparison

real_remote_2k.note: remote EOS file (root:// URL), 2,000 events, cache disabled, M1 workload reproduction; syscalls are zero because remote reads go through the network plugin

notes: The baseline bytes per read are compressed basket sizes; the coordinate paths read raw fixed-width records, so they move more bytes per read with one request per event.
The mapped coordinate rows issue zero application-level read syscalls; the mapped pages are demand-paged once by the kernel with sequential locality.
The real remote run mixes media: the baseline reads the remote EOS file and the coordinate paths read the local store file. The same-media rows keep both on local disk.
The local full-file baseline is decompression CPU bound (cpu 182.9 s of wall 192.8 s), not I/O wait; the remote baseline is I/O wait bound (98.5 percent).
No end-to-end reproduction of the documented 14-hour production workload; these are full-dataset local and sliced remote measurements.
The wall-clock ratios at the 2,000-event slice are microbenchmark scale and indicative, not stable guarantees.
